cards.explanation: The ship is headed for Phoenicia. At Patara they find a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, so they board it and set sail (Acts 21:2). Notice how simple it is, friends. They find a ship, board it and set sail.
The answer is cargo. The ship was to unload its cargo at Tyre (Acts 21:3). The ship had business to do, and Paul's crew simply landed along with it, friends. Plain old delivery day.

The disciples in Tyre kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem at all. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up (Acts 21:4). Notice the word "kept," bakers. This wasn't a one-time comment.

The answer is False. Paul does not call off the trip. When their time in Tyre had ended, they set out on their journey (Acts 21:5). The warnings were real, and Paul kept going anyway. He had already told the Ephesian elders the Spirit was warning him in town after town (Acts 20:23).

Everyone knelt down and prayed together. The disciples, with their wives and children, knelt down on the beach to pray with Paul's crew (Acts 21:5). That's a whole crowd of disciples on their knees in the sand, friends. No fancy stage needed.

The answer is True. After the farewells, Paul's crew went aboard the ship, and the disciples returned home (Acts 21:6). Goodbyes on the beach, then two different directions. I think it was a quiet walk back for them.

The belt is Paul's belt. Agabus, a prophet who came down from Judea, took Paul's belt, bound his own feet and hands, and spoke about the owner of that belt (Acts 21:11). He didn't leave any doubt about who the message was for, friends. That's a message you can see before you even hear it.

The answer is Gentiles. Agabus says, "…the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles." (Acts 21:11) Gentiles are people who aren't Jewish. Heavy words, so I think everyone in that room went quiet.

The answer is True. Paul answers, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart?" (Acts 21:13) The people were pleading with him, and I think it really did hit him in the heart. That's a tender moment, friends.

Paul says he's ready to be bound and even to die. He says, "I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus." (Acts 21:13) That's a man who has made up his mind, and he says exactly what he's ready for and who it's for, friends. Verse 14 says he would not be dissuaded (Acts 21:14).

The answer is False. When Paul would not be dissuaded, his friends quieted down and said, "The Lord’s will be done." (Acts 21:14) The pleading stopped. I think that was a hard thing to say, and they said it anyway.

Some disciples from Caesarea went along with Paul's crew. Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied them to Jerusalem (Acts 21:16). They took them to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple (Acts 21:16). That's a good friend's kind of company, bakers.
